cases.title: Linux service outage
cases.brief: A simulated report service stopped after a scheduled update. Identify the evidence and choose a safe recovery recommendation.
commands: /var/reports/output owner=root group=reports mode=750; service account=reporter; groups=reporter
10:01 package update; 10:03 directory owner changed from reporter to root
remediation: Restore the approved service access using a reviewed permission change, then retest
Disable access controls globally
Delete reporting data
cases.explanation: The mock journal and directory permissions support a permission mismatch. Confirm approved ownership/privileges and verify service plus normal access after a controlled correction.

cases.title: Windows login alert
cases.brief: A fictional shared Windows PC reports failed authentication. Determine what the evidence supports.
commands: 13:00 login_failed user=student; 13:01 login_failed user=student; 13:06 login_success user=student
12:55 Defender signatures updated; no malware alert
student: standard user, enabled; admin: separate account
Host reachable; no unusual egress recorded in supplied window
diagnoses: Only login attempts and success are established; intent unknown
remediation: Publish the user's credentials
Review activity with the account owner and preserve relevant event records
Disable all Windows accounts
cases.explanation: Authentication records do not establish who performed the action. Scoped review with the owner is proportionate; avoid claiming a breach.

cases.title: DNS and gateway failure
cases.brief: A synthetic training client connects to Wi-Fi, but a course portal hostname does not work.
commands: 192.168.50.1 reachable; no packet loss in mock test
Second approved lab client uses DNS 192.168.50.54 and resolves correctly
diagnoses: Configured DNS resolver is the likely failure point
remediation: Verify and correct the authorized resolver setting, then retest DNS and site access
Reinstall the operating system
Turn off the organization's firewall
cases.explanation: A valid IP, working gateway and alternate working resolver support a scoped DNS configuration hypothesis.

cases.title: Windows service dependency failure
cases.brief: A fictional Windows payroll application stops after approved maintenance.
commands: PayrollApp service stopped; dependency DatabaseClient service unavailable
14:01 DatabaseClient failed: configuration path not found
diagnoses: Changed dependency configuration is the leading hypothesis
remediation: Review and restore approved dependency configuration, then retest both services
Disable all antivirus protection
Delete the payroll database
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Linux disk and inode investigation
cases.brief: A fictional Linux training service reports that it cannot create a new output file.
commands: writer: cannot create file: No space left on device
Synthetic inventory shows 210000 tiny cache files
No package or permission changes in this window
diagnoses: Inode exhaustion prevents creating new files
remediation: Review retention and safely clear only approved disposable cache, then verify inode use and file creation
Delete unrelated user files
Disable all audit logging
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Cloud access rule drift
cases.brief: A simulated cloud policy review finds that private submissions were mistakenly included in a broad read permission.
commands: 08:22 IAM policy expanded from public-images/* to *
No actual customer data exists in the exercise
diagnoses: A broad policy creates an unauthorized read path in the synthetic test
remediation: Restrict access to public-images only and verify both permitted and denied requests
Make all files writable to everyone
Delete all training audit records
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Web application session diagnosis
cases.brief: A test-only student application appears to remain signed in after its logout button is used.
commands: Logout hides profile menu and navigates to homepage
Mock API request with existing session still returns HTTP 200
On logout, active server sessions must be revoked
Synthetic account uses normal student role
No real production account details provided
diagnoses: The mock server continues accepting a session after logout
remediation: Invalidate the active session at the trusted service and verify it is rejected afterward
Only change logout button text
Publish the session value
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Phishing alert and change correlation
cases.brief: A synthetic SOC queue contains a suspicious payment message and unrelated software changes.
commands: Message requests urgent bank update through a supplied link
Supplier bank changes require verified callback to existing contact
Web app deployment at 12:00 unrelated to supplier records
No successful account compromise confirmed in supplied window
diagnoses: The application deployment caused the supplier request
Potential supplier impersonation requires independent verification
remediation: Hold payment change and verify using established supplier contact channels
Send an MFA code to the email sender
Approve based on the sender's logo
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Network segmentation fault
cases.brief: A synthetic office VLAN test shows a guest client unexpectedly reaching a mock internal finance API.
commands: Guest VLAN 20; finance VLAN 40; intended policy denies guest-to-finance
Synthetic guest -> finance API TCP 443: allowed
Firewall rule guest-to-any allow placed above guest-to-finance deny
Policy change approved only for guest internet access
diagnoses: Rule precedence allows an unintended guest-to-finance path
remediation: Review and correct firewall precedence, then test allowed internet and denied finance paths
Turn off all network security rules
Give guests a finance administrator account
cases.explanation: Compare the three relevant diagnostic outputs with the stated policy or expected service behavior. The resulting diagnosis is supported only for the synthetic case. Use a scoped change, preserve evidence and verify the original workflow.

cases.title: Intermittent portal availability
cases.brief: An isolated mock course portal fails for some users after a configuration change. You have a budget of three evidence requests. Select sources, infer the best-supported cause and choose a safe action.
commands: Client A gets HTTP 503; client B gets HTTP 200 via the same hostname
Load balancer backend A unhealthy; backend B healthy
Backend A reports connection pool exhausted after a deploy
Both clients resolve the intended training address
Database disk 27% full; no capacity alarm
diagnoses: A global DNS outage explains the split results
A backend-specific connection pool issue is the likely cause
remediation: Disable audit logs and wait
Review deployment and backend pool settings, restore approved baseline, then test both backends
Make all services public
cases.explanation: The differing backend states and the pool error support a backend-specific fault. DNS is functioning; controlled rollback and verification are appropriate.

cases.title: Unusual backup failure
cases.brief: A fictional backup reports success but recovery verification fails. Choose three informative sources and decide whether recovery can be trusted.
commands: Scheduled snapshot task completed successfully at 02:00
Disposable restore test failed: encryption key version unavailable
Backup key rotated yesterday; prior key version disabled
diagnoses: Recovery is blocked by unavailable key material despite a completed backup
remediation: Declare recovery verified because snapshot succeeded
Delete old encrypted archives
Restore authorized key access under approved recovery controls, then repeat a disposable restore
cases.explanation: A successful backup job does not prove restorability. The failed test and disabled key identify a recovery dependency.

cases.title: Competing sign-in hypotheses
cases.brief: A synthetic identity alert looks suspicious, but maintenance and user activity may explain it. Collect three targeted observations and avoid claiming an unproven breach.
commands: Seven failed sign-ins for trainee between 09:00 and 09:03
Trainee confirms testing a newly issued password after a scheduled reset
09:04 successful sign-in with phishing-resistant MFA from enrolled device
No endpoint detection in the supplied inspection window
No additional IP metadata in available records
diagnoses: These logs conclusively prove an attacker compromised the account
The observed pattern is consistent with authorized reset activity; malicious intent remains unproven
remediation: Record the corroboration, maintain reasonable monitoring and escalate only with new evidence
Disable the entire company identity system
Publish the employee's login details
cases.explanation: Owner corroboration and successful MFA suggest a benign explanation; no provided evidence proves a breach. Keep proportionate monitoring and preserve privacy.

cases.title: Enterprise identity: departed employee session
cases.brief: A fictional former employee's account is disabled, but a test session can still read a training resource. Choose only three evidence requests.
commands: Account disabled at 10:00 UTC; no new interactive logins permitted
Session issued 09:40; token expires 11:40; revocation event absent
10:15 API read accepted for existing bearer token
Employment ended at 09:55; manager notification received
VPN gateway is online; zero service alerts
diagnoses: Existing issued session remains valid despite account disablement
remediation: Disable application logging
Revoke active sessions and tokens using approved identity procedures, then verify denied access
Delete all employee records
cases.explanation: Directory disablement blocks some future authentication but does not necessarily revoke already issued application tokens. Correlate session lifetime and API result, revoke through the approved system, then verify with a scoped authorized test.

cases.title: Linux administration: service unavailable after reboot
cases.brief: A fictional service works when manually started but is not running after a lab virtual-machine reboot.
commands: systemctl status lab-api: inactive (dead) after boot
Previous manual start succeeded and returned status 200
remediation: Change ownership of every system file
Stop collecting system logs
Review expected startup policy, approve enabling the service, and verify boot behavior in the lab
cases.explanation: A disabled systemd unit does not automatically start at boot, even if a prior manual run worked. Verify the approved configuration and only change it under lab authorization.

cases.title: Web API: cross-tenant data permission
cases.brief: A fabricated multi-tenant app identifies both users but appears to return another tenant's invoice. Select the most discriminating evidence.
commands: Approved synthetic GET /api/invoices/INV-B42 by A-17 returned 200 with invoice body
The app's navigation hides B42 from tenant A
diagnoses: A styling bug is the primary security issue
Server-side object authorization is not enforced for this resource
The user's MFA device is expired
remediation: Require server-side tenant/object authorization for each request and regression-test allow and deny cases
Hide invoice links in the browser only
Share the affected invoice publicly for easier debugging
cases.explanation: Authentication and a hidden UI link are insufficient. The resource owner and observed synthetic cross-tenant response support an object-level authorization weakness, requiring server-side enforcement.

cases.title: Cloud security: public storage policy regression
cases.brief: After a fictional infrastructure update, an intended-private reports object is accessible anonymously in a simulated policy test.
commands: Synthetic unauthenticated read: HTTP 200 for reports/customer-q4.csv
Monthly cloud expense remained within budget
The bucket is hosted in expected region
diagnoses: Access policy allows anonymous reads of classified internal data
Cloud cost overruns caused the data exposure
remediation: Approve a narrowly scoped policy correction and rerun anonymous-deny plus authorized-allow validation
Delete all reports without preservation
Disable all audit logs
cases.explanation: Broad principal grants plus internal classification and a synthetic anonymous success support a policy-scope defect. Restrict access through change control and test both denied and approved users.
